get.summary: Documentation-only operation for the mounted reading-graph read.
get.description: Owner-scoped projection of the complete Option E graph. A persisted cycle is isolated to its affected Threads and Reading Lists; every cycle edge names its series, issue and stored origin. The read-only frontier audit names current unread frontiers that Option E would offer while inert legacy or converted dependency evidence still records possible reader intent; the report is manual-review evidence only (#4198).

200.description: Graph status, cycles and safe repair options

get.summary: Documentation-only operation used to emit the generated OpenAPI contract.

post.summary:
Documentation-only operation for the AIP-133 standard Create on the v2
threads collection (#5702). The handler lives in `thread_lifecycle` and
shares the legacy write path; only the URL and the `Location` response
header differ.
post.description: Create a thread at the end of the authenticated reader's queue. The created resource (including its stable `id`) is returned at 201 with a `Location` header naming the v2 collection member. The write preserves owner assignment, the five-second duplicate-merge guard and the Python validation envelope; it creates no Plan, dependency or issue rows.

201.description: Created (or the duplicate created seconds earlier)

delete.description: Delete an owned Thread (AIP-135). A second delete, or a delete of a foreign or already deleted Thread, returns 404. Never 403.

patch.description: Partially update an owned Thread (AIP-134). Omitted fields are preserved. When `update_mask` is supplied only its fields are applied; a masked field missing from the body is cleared. An `expected` precondition that no longer matches the committed row returns 409 with `detail.code = thread_edit_conflict` and the current values. Foreign or deleted Threads return 404, never 403.

404.description: Thread not found (including another reader's thread)

409.description: Stale `expected` precondition; reload before retrying

put.summary: Documentation-only operation for the mounted issue-order resource.
put.description: Replace the complete issue order atomically. The projected Option E graph is validated before commit, so a manual reorder cannot introduce a strict-list/series-order cycle.

400.description: issue_ids must contain every thread issue exactly once

409.description: Projected reading graph would cycle; nothing was changed

post.summary: Documentation-only operation for the mounted issue-create resource.
post.description: Create issue labels atomically. Natural numeric placement never re-sorts previously persisted issues; a non-monotonic series appends without changing existing relative order. The complete reading graph is validated before commit.

400.description: Invalid issue range or no new issues

409.description: Projected reading graph would cycle; nothing was changed

post.summary: Documentation-only operation for the mounted issue-create preview resource.
post.description: Preview an issue-create edit before commit. Returns the safe default outcome and, when relevant, a numeric-resort outcome with exact before/after order and graph validation.

400.description: Invalid issue range or no new issues

post.summary: Documentation-only operation for the delete/reorder structure preview.
post.description: Preview a delete or reorder edit before commit. Returns exact before/after issues, list memberships, read/rating/identity state, affected Queue/Roll frontier, duplicate risk and projected graph conflicts.

restored.description:
True when the pending roll and die were restored; false when only the
snooze was removed (older snooze, later die choice, or an already-removed
snooze replayed after a lost response).

UserPreferencesPatchRequest.description:
Partial update of the authenticated user's preferences.

`theme` is optional: when omitted or explicit JSON null the current
preference is left unchanged and a missing row is seeded with the
default, exactly like the Python `UserPreferencesPatchRequest`.

UserPreferencesResponse.description: Current preference values for the authenticated user.

UserResponse.description: Response body for the current-user endpoint.
